## First Solar CEO Urges Bipartisan Support for Industrial Strategy, Enforcement of US Trade and Tax Policy at House Select Committee on China Hearing


November 20, 2026


Mark Widmar testifies at hearing on “ *Outproducing the CCP: Restoring American Manufacturing”*


WASHINGTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Mark Widmar, chief executive officer of First Solar, Inc. (Nasdaq: FSLR) (“First Solar” or “the Company”), today urged bipartisan support for an industrial strategy and the enforcement of American trade and tax laws to sustain domestic manufacturing growth.


At the invitation of Chairman John Moolenaar (R-Mich.), Widmar testified before the United States House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition Between the United States and the Chinese Communist Party (the House Select Committee on China).


Addressing the committee at the hearing on “ *Outproducing the CCP: Restoring American Manufacturing* , *”* Widmar said, “American technology, American factories, American workers, and consistent enforcement of our trade and tax laws are not Democratic priorities or Republican ones. They are American ones.”


First Solar is the country’s leading PV solar technology and manufacturing company and the only one of the world’s largest solar manufacturers to be headquartered in the US. The Company operates six manufacturing facilities in Alabama, Louisiana, Ohio, and South Carolina; R&D centers in Ohio and California; and a solar technology testing center in Arizona. By the end of 2026, First Solar expects to have invested over $5 billion in American manufacturing and R&D infrastructure since 2019, and by 2027 it forecasts approximately 17 GW of US nameplate module manufacturing capacity.


“First Solar is here as proof that America can rebuild manufacturing capacity,” Widmar said. “We didn’t invest approximately $5 billion in American manufacturing because it was easy. We invested because we believe in the American worker.”


Citing tax and trade policies across multiple administrations that catalyzed domestic solar manufacturing growth, Widmar noted, “The lesson is that industrial strategy must be bipartisan. When the rules hold from one Administration and Congress to the next, entire markets can grow, and domestic manufacturers can invest with certainty in the United States.”


Widmar noted the range of trade remedies available to help level the playing field for American workers and manufacturers and cited the Section 232 action on polysilicon as an example of a targeted remedy — one aimed at a specific national security risk or economic abuse and applied where there is domestic capacity to build. He said, “On behalf of all of our American workers, I thank President Trump and Secretary Lutnick for the first true acknowledgment that the solar supply chain is a national security issue.”


The full hearing is available on demand[here](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.youtube.com%2Fwatch%3Fv%3Dzj0XEwDZ5fs&esheet=54644436&newsitemid=20261120395166&lan=en-US&anchor=here&index=1&md5=56c2af415309809764c0ef04380d6e1c) .


**About First Solar, Inc.**


First Solar, Inc. is America’s leading PV solar technology and manufacturing company. The only US-headquartered company among the world’s largest solar manufacturers, First Solar is focused on competitively and reliably enabling power generation needs with its advanced, uniquely American thin film PV technology. Developed at R&D labs in California and Ohio, the Company’s technology provides a competitive, high-performance, and responsibly produced alternative to conventional crystalline silicon PV modules. For more information, please visit[www.firstsolar.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.firstsolar.com&esheet=54644436&newsitemid=20261120395166&lan=en-US&anchor=www.firstsolar.com&index=2&md5=8c69cf16d1b82fa52633a29db77b492d) .
